subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which identity should be authoritative when a QQBot C2C approval is delivered without an explicit allowFrom or execApprovals.approvers entry?
rationale: Current documentation and the shipped security fix require a configured approver, while the reported workflow asks to treat a direct chat itself as authorization; choosing a safe replacement identity is a security-policy decision.

options.title: Preserve explicit approvers
options.body: Keep the current allowFrom or execApprovals.approvers requirement and improve rejection/setup guidance so users do not wait for a timeout.

options.title: Bind the delivered recipient
options.body: Define the exact delivered or initiating C2C identity as the approver and require a narrow implementation plus negative cross-sender proof before changing the documented contract.

options.title: Close this direction
options.body: Reject implicit open-DM approval and direct the linked issue to the existing explicit approver configuration path.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit approvers
recommendation.body: Keep the current allowFrom or execApprovals.approvers requirement and improve rejection/setup guidance so users do not wait for a timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: The published QQBot approval advisory is the strongest available ownership signal for deciding whether this security boundary may change.
